title: Victorian pool gates, doors and self-closing latches
audience: Pool service workers, barrier inspectors and installers in Victoria. Gate and door work on barriers is building work needing a permit. The rules are Victorian.
learningOutcomes: State what the note requires of a pool gate's closing and latching, and explain what a failure shows.
Identify the door arrangements the note allows, and those it rules out, for outdoor and indoor pools.
Explain why child-resistant doorsets are limited to indoor pools.

instruction.heading: Gates must shut and latch unaided
instruction.body: SP 02 says gates must be self-closing and self-latching under AS 1926.1-2012. A gate that does not close and latch itself leaves the barrier open, so release each gate from the open position and check that it closes and latches itself.

instruction.heading: Gate posts and footings
instruction.body: Moving posts can stop a gate from latching. SP 02 says footings for posts and gates should be poured monolithically or as one footing across the opening, which keeps the posts from spreading and the gate from failing to latch. Record any gate that swings loose between its posts as a defect.

instruction.heading: Garages, sheds and building doors
instruction.body: SP 02 says tool sheds, garages and barbecues should sit outside the pool area, citing AS 1926.2-2007, Appendix B. Access to an outdoor pool must not be directly available through a building door, so a door from the house or a garage opening into the pool area does not meet the rule.

instruction.heading: Doors leading out of a building
instruction.body: Child-resistant doorsets may only be used for indoor pools and the indoor part of a combined indoor and outdoor pool, so they must stay out of barriers that protect outdoor water. A new outdoor pool or spa area must not be directly accessible from a building.

instruction.heading: Indoor pools and side-hung doors
instruction.body: SP 02 says an indoor pool is fully enclosed by walls on all sides, roofed, and accessed from within the building. A side-hung door used as part of an indoor pool barrier must swing away from the pool, be self-closing and self-latching, and have a non-climbable zone on its outside. Permit drawings for indoor pools must show the barrier, child-resistant doorsets and the door swing direction.

procedure: Establish if the swing gate or hinged door forms part of the enclosure, and if the pool is indoor or outdoor.
Open the gate fully, release it, and check it closes and latches itself.
Check the post and footing arrangement, and record any movement that could stop the gate latching.
Check door arrangements against the outdoor or indoor rules, and record any door that opens straight onto the pool zone.

workedExamples.situation: On an outdoor pool, the gate closes but does not latch itself when released, and it latches only when pushed by hand. A family's back door opens straight onto the pool zone.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What must be reported, and what should not be done?
workedExamples.reasoning: Both faults are barrier concerns under SP 02. The gate does not latch itself, and the back door gives direct access to an outdoor pool. Do not adjust the gate or seal the door as a quick fix, since that work is building work needing a permit. Put both faults in writing to the owner, copying the building surveyor, and keep small children clear of the water until it complies.

commonErrors.error: Propping a gate open for convenience.
commonErrors.prevention: A propped gate has failed the barrier. Report it and keep the gate closed.

commonErrors.error: Using a child-resistant door set on an outdoor pool.
commonErrors.prevention: Child-resistant doorsets are only for indoor pools and the indoor part of combined pools. Report such a door on an outdoor pool.

commonErrors.error: Accepting a gate that latches only when pushed by hand.
commonErrors.prevention: Release the gate from the open position and check that it closes and latches itself.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: A gate or door that does not latch itself lets small children reach the water. Keep children clear of the water until the swing gate or hinged door complies.
Altering or replacing barrier gates and doors is building work that needs a permit in Victoria. Builder registration may apply. This lesson grants neither.
Figures are Victorian (VBA Building Practice Note SP 02, 2023). The named standards, the 2012 edition of AS 1926.1 and AS 1288, were not read.

qualityStandard: Each gate is recorded as closing and latching itself after release.
Each door in the barrier is recorded as meeting the outdoor or indoor rule, or reported.
documentationEvidence: Gate test record with position tested and result
Door arrangement record with indoor or outdoor status and direct-access check
Defect notice copied to the owner and building surveyor
summary: Gates must be self-closing and self-latching under AS 1926.1-2012.
Child-resistant doorsets are for indoor pools only, and an outdoor pool must not be directly accessible from a building.
Garages, sheds and barbecues should sit outside the pool area.

knowledgeChecks.question: What load does the note place on the top of a mesh barrier panel?
Can a child-resistant doorset open from a building onto an outdoor pool?
options: Yes, when the doorset is fitted with a self-closing hinge and it is locked at night
Only if it is painted and the paint is bright, new and glossy for the pool
No, child-resistant doorsets cannot form any portion of a fence around outdoor water
Only on Sundays, when the building is quiet and the gate is open today

knowledgeChecks.question: Under SP 02, what must a side-hung door used as part of an indoor pool barrier do?
options: Stay open for airflow and the door is left unlatched
Swing away from the pool and be self-closing and self-latching
Open into the pool area for rescue access and stay open for rescue staff
Have no non-climbable zone on its outside and open out onto the deck

sourceReferences: Victorian Building Authority, Building Practice Note SP 02, Swimming pool barriers and other requirements (Version 3, 26 September 2023), gate, footing, garage and shed, child-resistant doorset and indoor pool sections; rights: user-held; reworded (no copying). The gate load test and the powered-door points previously attributed to Practice Note 05-2018 are not in SP 02.

Priority: official Victorian Building Authority source. It overrides other pool sources on the points it covers, for Victoria only. Dated: 26 September 2023 (Version 3); read through a summary tool on 2026-11-03. Victorian requirement. UNCONFIRMED for other states and territories, and the current edition of AS 1926.1 is UNCONFIRMED.

UNCONFIRMED: named standards, the 2012 edition of AS 1926.1 and AS 1288 (text not read); door and gate rules in other states and territories. Powered-door rules (knowledge check 3) are not stated in SP 02 and remain UNCONFIRMED.

officialReferences.title: Pool safety barriers (Victorian Building Authority)
officialReferences.covers: Read via summary fetch. New pools and spas must have self-latching and self-closing pool gates. A new outdoor pool or spa area must not be directly accessible via a building. Barriers must comply with AS 1926.1-2012, and the page gives separate checklists for pools installed on 8 April 1991, 30 April 2010 and 1 May 2010. Victoria only. Not confirmed by this page: Practice Note 05-2018 itself (not located in this session), the 25 kg gate load test, the single footing advice, the rules for garage, shed and roller doors, and whether building work permits apply to altering barriers.

officialReferences.title: Building Practice Note SP 02, Swimming pool barriers and other requirements (Victorian Building Authority), Version 3
officialReferences.covers: Building Practice Note SP 02 (VBA), Version 3, published 26 September 2023; the note shows no review date. It covers self-closing and self-latching gates under AS 1926.1-2012, the gate footing rule, tool sheds, garages and barbecues outside the pool area, child-resistant doorsets limited to indoor pools, and a 25 kg weight on the top of a mesh barrier not reducing its height below 1200 mm. The note does not state a 25 kg gate load test or powered-door fail-safe rules: those points remain UNCONFIRMED.
